hints: Focus on what each test is telling you separately, one test for a functional group and one test for reactivity.
Fumes of $\text{HCl}$ with $\text{PCl}_5$ means Q must contain an $\text{-OH}$ group, so rule out any molecule without one.
Turning orange dichromate(VI) green means Q is easily oxidised, so decide which $\text{-OH}$ containing compound can still be oxidised further.
walkthrough:
**Decode the phosphorus pentachloride test**

Think of $\text{PCl}_5$ as an $\text{-OH}$ detector. Alcohols and carboxylic acids both react to release steamy fumes of $\text{HCl}$.

$$\text{R-OH} + \text{PCl}_5 \rightarrow \text{R-Cl} + \text{POCl}_3 + \text{HCl}$$

**Decode the dichromate test**

Think of acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ as an oxidising agent test. Orange $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ turning green to $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ means Q has been oxidised.

$$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} \text{(orange)} \rightarrow \text{Cr}^{3+} \text{(green)}$$

**Combine both clues to find Q**

Q must have $\text{-OH}$ AND be oxidisable. A secondary alcohol fits perfectly because it has $\text{-OH}$ for the first test and is oxidised to a ketone for the second test.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ is propanal, an aldehyde with no $\text{-OH}$ group, so it gives no $\text{HCl}$ fumes with $\text{PCl}_5$. It would turn dichromate green by oxidation to propanoic acid, but it fails the first test.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ is propanoic acid and does give $\text{HCl}$ fumes with $\text{PCl}_5$ due to its $\text{-OH}$. However, a carboxylic acid is already fully oxidised and cannot be oxidised further, so dichromate stays orange.
options.C: Correct. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ is propan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol. Its $\text{-OH}$ gives $\text{HCl}$ fumes with $\text{PCl}_5$, and warming with acidified dichromate oxidises it to propanone, turning the solution from orange to green.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{COH}$ is 2-methylpropan-2-ol, a tertiary alcohol. It does give $\text{HCl}$ fumes with $\text{PCl}_5$, but tertiary alcohols resist oxidation because there is no hydrogen on the carbon bearing the $\text{-OH}$, so dichromate stays orange.
